messages:
mike: Heads-up — console charts started stuttering for large-org queries after the last canary. Anyone else seeing sustained 200–400ms main-thread spikes?
anya: saw it on /dashboards/usage at ~11:24. LCP jumped from ~1.1s to ~2.4s for big tables. spikes line up with the bundle-splitting change.
raj: same. reproduces in prod-canary for accounts with >200k events. suspect prefetch ordering changed when we flipped to async chunk loads.
mike: here's the perf-bot flame link: https://graf.redwood/perf/abc123 (main thread dominated by Chart.draw)
perf-bot: summary -> main-thread CPU: 48% in Chart.draw; KVCache.init latency +120ms at 95p; chunk-4 fetchs show higher RTTs and timeouts.
liz: bundle diffs look odd — chunk-4 (charting code) increased by ~45KB after the split. also prefetch headers changed.
sam: can reproduce locally with the big-org fixture, will run the canary repro script and post traces.
raj: quick repro steps:
1. login as big account
2. open dashboard with timeframe > 90d
3. open sparklines panel
Observation: first chart paint blocks until chunk-4 fetch finishes, even though KV cache should be primed.
mike: minimal stack from devtools:
```
fetch("/static/chunk-4.js") -> eval -> Chart.render -> KVCache.init -> window.requestIdleCallback starvation
```
anya: this smells like the affinity/prefetch change we merged — we now set X-Prefetch-Affinity: remote for low-capacity routes, which may delay local kvcache priming.
sam: FYI deploy-bot reported a canary started at 2523456700 (canary-id: can-2026-03-20-11). seeing client-timeout spikes for chunk4 on that canary.
deploy-bot: Canary can-2026-03-20-11: 12% chunk4 client-timeout errors in last 5m. auto-rollback threshold = 10%.
mike: propose two quick mitigations: rollback the affinity header change OR add rel=preload for chunk-4 on dashboard route so parsing isn't blocked. rollback is fastest.
liz: alternative less-blasty: mark chunk-4 as highPriority and use <link rel=preload> for route-only. cheaper than reverting split.
raj: I still think the root is prefetch affinity — prefetches routed remote don't hit local CDN priming, so kvcache isn't warm. we should revert the affinity tweak for the dashboard route.
anya: agree. let's A/B the fix: revert affinity for 50% of traffic and add preload for 50% to compare metrics. need short window and clear KPIs (main-thread 95p, LCP, chunk4 error rate).
sam: spinning canary with revert+preload now (can-2026-03-20-11b). will report after 15m.
sam: (15m later) can-2026-03-20-11b results: main-thread 95p dropped 400ms -> 120ms, LCP back to ~1.2s, chunk4 errors 0.5%. stable for 15m.
mike: awesome. push canary-2 to wider traffic for 30m. If it holds, roll out revert and landing patch for selective preload.
raj: created ticket INF-3172: "chart chunk prefetch affinity caused kvcache priming regressions" with traces and repro.
anya: adding followup: instrument per-route kvcache priming metrics and add unit test that simulates remote-prefetch -> ensure preload fallback.
liz: also vendor note: check CDN edge config for stale cache headers that might magnify remote prefetch penalty.
mike: great triage. thanks everyone — rollback plan if canary-2 shows regressions. :thumbsup:
